title: Liectroux Robot Vacuums Compared: C30B vs X6 vs M7S Pro vs M70 Pro
metaDescription: Comparing four Liectroux robot vacuums: AI map vs LDS laser vs lidar navigation, self-emptying vs manual, and vacuum-only vs vacuum-and-mop combo — which model fits your home.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: Liectroux sits in the budget-to-midrange bracket of robot vacuums — well below the self-cleaning, camera-navigation flagships from Narwal or Roborock, but with enough range across its own lineup that picking the right model still matters. The four models here span three different navigation systems and the gap between a basic vacuum-only bot and a self-emptying vacuum-and-mop combo. If you want the top-end self-washing-mop experience, our [Narwal Freo Z10 review](/blog/narwal-freo-z10-robot-vacuum-mop-review-2026/) covers that tier — this guide is about getting the most out of a more modest budget.

items.label: C30B — Navigation
items.value: AI Map Navigation, smart partitioning, electric water tank (vacuum + basic mop)

items.label: X6 — Navigation
items.value: LDS Laser Navigation, saves up to 5 floor maps, 6500Pa suction

items.label: M70 Pro — Navigation
items.value: Lidar navigation, multi-floor map storage, self-emptying dustbin, 175-min runtime

items.label: Suction Power
items.value: 6000-6500Pa across all four — the real differentiator is navigation and maintenance, not suction

items.label: Maintenance
items.value: C30B/X6/M7S Pro: manual dustbin emptying — M70 Pro: self-emptying base station

pros: All four hit 6000Pa+ suction, which is genuinely strong for hard floors and low-pile carpet regardless of which model you pick
LDS laser and lidar navigation (X6, M70 Pro) map rooms more precisely than basic AI camera mapping, meaning fewer missed spots and cleaner room boundaries
The M70 Pro's self-emptying base means weeks between having to touch the dustbin — a real convenience upgrade over the other three
Multi-floor map storage on the M70 Pro is genuinely useful in two-story homes — it remembers each floor's layout instead of re-mapping every time
Even the entry C30B includes basic mopping via an electric water tank, not just vacuuming
cons: None of these four have camera-based obstacle recognition — expect the occasional missed cable or pet toy that a camera-equipped flagship would avoid
The self-emptying M70 Pro base station takes real counter/floor space and needs to sit near an outlet, same trade-off as pricier brands
Mopping on the C30B/M7S Pro is basic pad-drag style, not the spinning, self-washing mop system found on premium models like the Narwal Freo Z10
5-map storage on the X6 sounds generous but most single-floor homes only ever use one — it matters mainly for multi-floor households

items.question: Which Liectroux robot vacuum should I choose?
items.answer: For a single-floor apartment on a tight budget, the C30B covers vacuuming and basic mopping well. If precise room mapping matters more than price, the X6's LDS laser navigation is the step up. If you want a true 2-in-1 vacuum-and-mop without stepping up to self-emptying, the M7S Pro is the balance point. If hands-off maintenance is the priority and budget allows it, the M70 Pro's self-emptying base and lidar navigation is the one to get.

items.question: Is a robot vacuum with lidar navigation worth it over a cheaper laser or camera model?
items.answer: Lidar (on the M70 Pro here) generally maps more accurately in low light and around furniture edges than basic camera-based AI mapping, and it tends to be more consistent between cleaning runs. If your home has a lot of furniture legs, varied lighting, or multiple floors, the more precise navigation genuinely reduces missed spots and re-cleaning. For a small, simply laid-out apartment, the difference matters less.

items.question: Do I need a self-emptying robot vacuum?
items.answer: It depends on how much you mind emptying a dustbin every few days versus every few weeks. The M70 Pro's self-emptying base is a real quality-of-life upgrade for busy households or anyone with pets shedding heavily, but it's not essential — the other three models work fine with manual emptying if you don't mind the extra five minutes a week.

items.question: Are Liectroux robot vacuums good for pet hair?
items.answer: At 6000-6500Pa suction, all four handle pet hair on hard floors and low-pile carpet reasonably well. For heavy shedding, the M70 Pro's larger 3L dust bag and self-emptying base mean you're not stopping to clear a tangled brush or full bin as often, which matters more in pet households than the suction number alone.

sections.content: The suction numbers barely separate these four — the real decision is navigation precision and how much maintenance you're willing to do by hand. Budget and simple: C30B. Best mapping for the price: X6. Balanced 2-in-1: M7S Pro. Least hands-on: M70 Pro. If none of these feel like enough and you want a genuinely self-washing mop system, that's a different budget tier entirely — worth comparing against the Narwal Freo Z10 before deciding.
